newsitem.title: USA: Texas spot power surges on cold weather, natgas.
newsitem.headline: Texas spot power surges on cold weather, natgas.

text.p: Spot wholesale electricity prices in the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) were sharply higher Monday due to the much below-normal temperatures in the state and the resulting stronger natural gas market, sources said.
"They burn more natural gas here. With those prices so high, electricity was bound to jump," one market source said.

Temperatures through the state were forecast to drop to 10 to 20 degrees Fahrenheit below-normal Tuesday and then 20 to 30 degrees below-normal Wednesday. The cold is expected to last through at least the early part of next week.
ERCOT firm, peak power for a 16-hour block for Tuesday delivery was much higher in the $42.00-43.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) range, as compared with Friday's $31.00-32.00 trading range.
Non-firm peak power was pegged at $40.00-41.00, also up more than $10 from deals done Friday in the $27.00-28.00 range.
Firm off-peak ERCOT power transactions were talked in the $17.00-19.00 range, up sharply from Friday's $11.00-13.00 trading range.
Non-firm off-peak ERCOT power was assessed at $14.00-16.00, up from $9.00-11.00 evident on Friday.

As short-term prices gained significant ground and the futures markets surged, ERCOT January/February peak power prices moved into the $38.00-39.00 range, as compared with $34.00-34.50 seen on Friday.
Like electricity, natural gas prices in south Texas rose by about 50 cents to the $3.90s to around $4 per million British thermal units.
